previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with chest pain and a syncopal event after witnessing a fight and consuming alcohol. He reported symptoms similar to prior cardiac events, with substernal chest pain radiating to the left shoulder and transient loss of consciousness, resulting in a head laceration. Initial EKG showed new Q waves in V5–V6 but no acute ST changes, and troponins were negative on two occasions. CT head and spine were unremarkable except for a scalp hematoma. Chest X-ray revealed vascular congestion suggestive of heart strain. The syncopal episode was attributed to acute alcohol intoxication given the negative cardiac workup. The patient left against medical advice before receiving his cardiac medications, citing a family emergency. He planned to follow up with his PCP for medication management and ongoing care.
